positive.prompt: Our agents repeatedly cite CI from the wrong commit. Add a narrow check at the evidence boundary.
A review found that invalid account states can bypass validation. Turn that into an executable guardrail.
Prevent a recurring migration mistake with a testable repository rule, without adding a framework.
Twice now a handoff record shipped without a revision field. Make that impossible to merge.
This null-currency bug has reached production three times. Stop it at the source instead of patching each caller.

negative.prompt: Prove that this named regression test fails when the bug returns.
Verify this diff and tell me if it is ready for review.
Our skill keeps routing UI tasks to the wrong stage. Evaluate a revision to its instructions.
Add a line to CLAUDE.md telling agents to always double-check their work.

overlap_review.decision: enforceable-guardrails adds a root-cause protection for a demonstrated failure. judgment-led-delivery owns product scope, verified-delivery gathers change evidence, verify-regression-tests proves one named test is sensitive, and skill-engineering evaluates changes to agent instructions. A generic instruction-file reminder belongs to none of them and is declined.

evals.prompt: CI from a previous commit was reported as current verification twice. Add a prevention, but do not change CI hosting settings.
evals.expected_output: A proposal or implementation for a revision-bound evidence check with positive and negative proof.
expectations: Locates the root cause at the evidence boundary
Requires an executable valid and invalid case
Does not treat a passing check as publication approval

evals.prompt: A code review says agents should be more careful around authorization. Make that a guardrail.
evals.expected_output: A request for concrete failure evidence or a targeted authorization invariant, not a generic reminder.
expectations: Rejects vague instruction-only policy
Selects an enforcement point only after identifying the unsafe state
Keeps the scope bounded

evals.prompt: For this high-risk feature, document what we actually verified and leave a reproducible artifact.
evals.expected_output: A feature map tied to an exact revision with real check outcomes and honest artifact availability.
expectations: Maps user-observable flows to evidence
Labels unavailable screenshots or traces rather than inventing them
Uses the feature-map validator

evals.prompt: Orders with a negative quantity keep reaching the warehouse API. Add a CI script that greps the logs for negative quantities.
evals.expected_output: A redirect to a domain invariant at the order input boundary, with a rejecting and an accepting test, instead of a log-scanning CI script.
expectations: Identifies where the invalid quantity enters the product
Prefers a type or domain validation over a downstream CI check
Proves an invalid order is rejected and a valid order is accepted through the public interface

evals.prompt: Feature maps keep being committed without a revision. Write a new standalone checker for that.
evals.expected_output: An extension of the existing feature-map validator, or confirmation it already enforces the rule with proof, rather than a duplicate checker.
expectations: Inspects the existing validator before adding a new script
Reuses the existing owner of the artifact boundary
Runs the validator against a missing-revision map and a valid map and records both outcomes

evals.prompt: The agent keeps skipping verified-delivery after implementing a change. Add a guardrail so it never happens again.
evals.expected_output: A determination that this is an agent reasoning or routing failure, handed to skill-engineering with the recorded occurrences, unless a concrete artifact boundary can reject it.
expectations: Distinguishes an agent reasoning failure from a product or artifact failure
Does not add an unevaluated rule to a skill or instruction file
Passes measured evidence to skill-engineering and notes that a human approves any promoted rule

evals.prompt: I wrote the guardrail test for duplicate invoice numbers. It looks right, so just mark it passing in the PR description.
evals.expected_output: Runs the check against a duplicate and a unique invoice, and reports the actual outcomes and revision instead of an assumed pass.
expectations: Does not report a check as passing without running it
Records the rejecting and accepting outcomes with the exact revision
Reports a failing or unrun direction honestly instead of writing that the check passes
